## Design

### 2026-10-08 – October 7: Got a Linux desktop running on my Android!!

**2.5h**

October 7: Got a Linux desktop running on my Android!!
I wanted to dual boot Linux Mint on my Android device because I already had the ISO. Turns out that's basically impossible. My phone has an ARM chip, and the Mint ISO is built for x86 PCs. After watching a few YouTube videos and reading around on Google, I decided to go with Termux + proot-distro, which runs Debian inside Android without root.

It didn't go smoothly at first. apt couldn't find xfce4 because I forgot to run apt update. Then Termux said the "debian" container wasn't installed, so I had to reinstall it. I also got a scary red "Failed to scan devices: Permission denied" message, but a quick Google search showed it's harmless.

The next mistake was mine: I typed my start script into the terminal that was already running the desktop, so nothing got saved. Then pasting the script with extra spaces broke the file. I fixed it by checking which prompt I was in and recreating the script properly. After that, XFCE appeared in Termux:X11. Can't believe it actually works!

The actual reason why I had to do this is my laptop was really old, and it was not able to run kicad which is important for this week project. So I hope even this hours are considered in the project hours

![Screenshot_20261007-230642](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YOtDeK4Mo59LYLbUJcJzTXj9keV6paCT/018033413195795906039aae4a283fa5e9f9dd533303e214d83aa2c850ae61a5.png)

The tl;dr: Mint can't dual boot on ARM phones, but Termux + proot-distro + Debian + XFCE + Termux:X11 gives you a full Linux desktop. Always run apt update first.

Time spent this session: about 2.5 hours
